cues.en: So using paid router outlet is a crucial part of setting up navigation in a native script app because
it enables that stack based navigation, which is such a core feature of native mobile apps.
Now, Native Script does not only give us a page throughout our outlet, it also gives us a separate
router object which can do a bit more than the default angular router.
As you can see, this works absolutely fine and therefore there is no reason to not use it except for
when you need certain special functionalities.
And one of them could be that, especially for that off page, you don't really want to be able to go
back.
Right.
If you did log in, you want to move to a new page.
But going back should not be enabled because you are locked in.
There should be no backwards navigation.
There should be no back button on the to do page.
And for that, what we essentially want to do is we want to clear that stack of pages and not just push
a new page on it.
But I actually have this being the only page, the new page for a new stack of pages, you could say.
So essentially our off page should be removed from the stack of pages once we navigate it away from
it.

Angular router.

So this is all important to understand that we have this special routers, extended router here, so
